text.en:
Meena heard a plink, plink, plink in the kitchen. A tap was dripping.
"It is only a few drops," said her brother.
Meena put a bucket under it. By evening the bucket was half full!
"Little drops add up," she said.

We get water from rivers, wells, ponds, rain and taps.
We use water for drinking, cooking, bathing, washing and watering plants.
Water is precious. Clean water is not easy to find, and we must not waste it.
We can save water: close the tap while brushing, fix leaking taps, use a bucket to bathe, and reuse water to water plants.
Where does water come from? From rivers, wells, ponds, rain, and then through pipes to our taps.
We use water to drink, cook, wash and water plants. Every living thing needs water.
A dripping tap wastes many glasses of water every day. Fix it, or close it tightly.
Brush with the tap closed. Bathe with a bucket. Water the plants with leftover water.

problem.en: Ravi lets the tap run for 2 minutes while brushing. Meena closes it. Who saves more water, and how?

text.en: Ravi keeps the tap open the whole time. Water flows and goes down the drain.

why.en: Running water that nobody uses is wasted.

text.en: Meena closes the tap while brushing and opens it only to rinse.

why.en: She uses only the water she needs.

prompt.en: Your cousin leaves the tap running while she washes her hands with soap. What will you tell her?

requiredIdeas.en: Water is precious and we should not waste it.
Close the tap while soaping, open it only to rinse.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a few drops do not matter.

points.en: We get water from rain, rivers, wells and ponds.
Water is precious. Do not waste it.
Close taps, fix leaks, use a bucket and reuse water.
